questions: At k=100 and k=1000, is the two-half filter faster than its control (cuda_range_prune_tm)?
At k=10, 100 and 1000, is it faster than v3, in one session?
prior_guess: faster than v3 at k=10 only; registered before the run
timing: 3 processes, 3 warm-up + 20 measured rounds, rotating order, batch 1, 256 threads, 64 seeds
queries: the 500 calibration queries only; the 6,480 are not used
correctness: two-half at each k: VERIFY=1 (IDs, scores and the pruning schedule against a CPU model) plus the CPU reference; control and v3 reuse da-02 and gsb-02. Every timing round of every configuration is compared with the CPU reference
eligibility: as 2026-11-23-gpusparse-k1000-batch amendments 1 and 2: 4.0 machine cores, 0.05 pinned core, no active foreign GPU process; ineligible processes kept and replaced; 10 quiet minutes after another user's job
decision_rule: descriptive only. Recommended configuration per k: the faster of two-half and v3 if the paired 95% interval excludes 1. No per-query selection is fitted
deadline: no process starts after 2026-11-24 23:00 EST; an incomplete run is recorded and not analysed
limits: calibration queries only, which chose the settings

amendments.registered: before any process of this experiment ran
amendments.change: k=10 dropped (6 configurations, not 8); 10 measured rounds, not 20; the quiet wait after another user's job is 2 minutes, not 10; no separate VERIFY stage and no smoke run
amendments.reason: submission deadline; k=10 was measured in #34, and the schedule model was verified there at k=10; the scorer sources are unchanged
amendments.consequence: answers are still compared with the CPU reference in every round of every process; the pruning schedule is not re-verified at k=100/1000; no k=10 comparison of two-half and v3 in one session; eligibility limits and statistics unchanged
